# Use eval-harness-generator

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Takes a skill's SKILL.md and generates a set of eval cases — trigger queries, expected output shape, and pass/fail criteria — ready to drop into the skill's evals/ directory.

**Reach for it when** adding evals to a new or existing skill, verifying a skill behaves as documented, or building a regression gate before modifying a skill.

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install eval-harness-generator                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install eval-harness-generator --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install eval-harness-generator --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the API builder pack: [`--pack api-builder`](../packs/use-the-api-builder-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "Write eval cases for this SKILL.md so I can put them in its evals folder"
- "Generate trigger queries and pass/fail criteria for the release-notes skill"
- "I'm about to edit a skill — build me a regression set from its SKILL.md first"
- "Check this skill behaves as documented: draft eval cases covering its anti-patterns"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "Design an eval harness for our customer-support chatbot's RAG pipeline"
- "Help me author a brand-new skilldrop skill from scratch, manifest and all"
- "We need a golden set and LLM-judge rubric for our summarization feature in production"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use eval-harness-generator".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **Triggers must be realistic.** A trigger of "run this skill" is not an eval case — it doesn't test anything specific. Each trigger should be the kind of input a real user would paste.
- **expected_shape items must be checkable.** "Output is good" is not checkable. "Output contains a numbered repro sequence starting from a clean state" is.
- **Cover the refusal cases.** The most common gap in skilldrop evals is missing cases for the skill's anti-patterns — the bad outputs the quality bar explicitly forbids. At least 2 of the 8–12 cases must test that the skill refuses or avoids its stated failure mode.
- **Don't pad to 12.** Eight strong cases beat twelve weak ones. Only add cases that test a distinct failure mode not already covered.
